procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
During the hearing the protest committee clarified in accordance with RRS 63.2(c) that the hearing request was not only a request for redress but also a protest, and proceeded with it accordingly.
facts: In race 3, during the first upwind leg, GBR 4013 was sailing on starboard tack on a close-hauled course on a collision course with IRL 5219 on port tack.
IRL 5219 bore away in an attempt to sail astern of GBR 4013. There was contact between the bow of IRL 5219 and the port quarter of GBR 4013.
The hull was punctured at the hull deck joint, resulting in the toe rail being cracked. There was also damage to two stanchions.
GBR 4013 checked the crew and the damage, plugged the hole, and retired from the race.
conclusions: IRL 5219, on port failed to keep clear of GBR 4013 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
IRL 5219 did not avoid contact with GBR 4013 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for GBR 4013 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with IRL 5219 when it became clear that IRL 5219 was not keeping clear. GBR 4013 did not break RRS 14(a).
IRL 5219 caused serious damage by her breach and took an appropriate penalty by retiring as required by RRS 44.1(b).

GBR 4013’s score in race 3 was made significantly worse through no fault of her own by physical damage because of the action of IRL 5219 that was breaking RRS 10 and 14 and took an appropriate penalty. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(2) are met.
decision: The protest is upheld. Since IRL 5219 took an applicable penalty, she is not further penalised under RRS 60.5(c)(2). Redress is given to GBR 4013. GBR 4013 is to be scored in race 3 points equal to the average, rounded to the nearest tenth of a point (0.05 to be rounded upward), of her points in all races sailed before the last scheduled day of the regatta, except race 3. No other boat’s score shall change.
